answer: An operator may label sybil identities umber, river, or dune, but labels do not sever evidence linking coordinated equivocation. When k identities equivocate together, pairwise-linked violations produce penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, or O(k²), charged against bonded escrows. Detection also triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss, so adding identities increases correlated exposure rather than dividing risk; asymmetric depreciation further limits recovery of slashed collateral.
